column1: # A2: verifier's blind number-and-word pairs from three crib despatches (rule for choosing them: crib_choice_rule.txt)
# FINDING BEFORE ANY PAIR: in none of the three is a word written over its own number. The English is running text in a
# second hand in the spaces between the number rows. In c36 (No. 5, 22 Jan 1778) and c185 (Private, 10 Apr 1778) the
# English lines are wider than the number rows and end before the numbers do (c185: 108 words over 93 numbers, the last
# 14 numbers under ruled strokes; c36: 44 words over 52 numbers). Only in c73 (No. 8, 16 Feb 1778) do the lines keep pace
# with the rows (catchwords 'publick/3613', 'holydays/99', 'situation/3381' at the page feet).
# My pre-stated rule (word squarely over number) therefore yields NO pair of grade H by position. What I can honestly offer:
#  M  = c73, a row whose line has exactly as many words as the row has numbers, counted off one to one
#  Ls = c73, first word of a line with first number of its row (counts unequal, so only the start is taken)
#  Lc = c36, counted off one to one from the sixth number (the first five stand before the English begins to fit; same
#       opening length as No. 35 where 717, which stands at 'I'/'me' three times in c73, is the sixth number)
#  R  = recurrence: the same number twice with one content word common to both places (c185)
# Forty per crib could not be reached in c36 (20) or c185 (5 occurrences of 3 numbers). I did not pad them.
# My expectation, written before comparison: M pairs right perhaps half the time, Ls and Lc less, because any spelled
# word or null in a row shifts everything after it; R pairs most likely right.
# columns: crib  row  pos  number  word  grade
